question: Covering an orchard against frost costs €1,000; an uncovered frost destroys €5,000 of fruit. Above what forecast chance of frost should the grower cover?
answer: Above 20%. Covering costs €1,000 every time; not covering costs €5,000 times the chance of frost. The two break even when that chance is 1,000 ÷ 5,000, one in five. By this cost–loss ratio, a 30% forecast is decisive for this grower. The covers go on under a sky that will probably stay clear.
move: Whether to act depends on the odds and on what each mistake costs.
ask: Before I act on a risk, have I weighed the odds against what each mistake would cost me?
trap: Waiting until frost is more likely than not before acting.

diagram.caption: Covers cost €1,000; frost costs €5,000 times its chance. Above 20%, covering is cheaper.

source: Katz & Murphy, Economic Value of Weather Forecasts
reference: Katz & Murphy (eds.), Economic Value of Weather and Climate Forecasts, Cambridge University Press, 1997
